link_notes: Repo is HALO_Inpatient (a reproduction repo for the preprint 'Synthesizing Extremely High Dimensional Electronic Health Records'), and the Nature Communications paper has no full text, so sources are thin.

open_release.rationale: The abstract frames the synthetic EHRs as privacy-preserving alternatives usable without privacy concerns.

quotes.text: Synthetic electronic health records (EHRs) that are both realistic and privacy-preserving offer alternatives to real EHRs for machine learning (ML) and statistical analysis.

pipeline_testing.rationale: Nothing in the sources points to this purpose.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The abstract reports that models trained on the synthetic data reach accuracy similar to models trained on real data.

quotes.text: also enhances the accuracy of predictive modeling and enables downstream ML models to attain similar accuracy as models trained on genuine data.

statistical_replication.rationale: The abstract claims preserved statistical properties and an R2 above 0.9 on code probabilities.

quotes.text: which preserve the statistical properties of real EHRs and can train accurate ML models without privacy concerns.

causal_inference.rationale: Nothing in the sources points to this purpose.

education.rationale: Nothing in the sources points to this purpose.

benchmarking.rationale: The README trains baseline models to compare against HALO, but no text shows HALO itself used as a baseline or benchmark.

quotes.text: Next, any desired baseline models may be trained by changing your working directory to `baselines/{baseline_model}` and running the corresponding `train_{baseline_model}.py` script

imbalance_correction.rationale: No full text is available, so any class-imbalance experiment cannot be ruled in or out.
